HLSHFO

This product covers the Hawaiian islands

**NOLO MOVING SLOWLY WESTWARD**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Hurricane Watch has been cancelled for Big Island East, Big
Island Interior, Big Island North, Big Island South, Big Island
Southeast, Big Island Summits, Kohala, and Kona

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Big Island East, Big
Island Interior, Big Island North, Big Island South, Big Island
Southeast, Big Island Summits, Kohala, and Kona
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Haleakala Summit,
Kahoolawe, Kipahulu, Lanai Leeward, Lanai Mauka, Lanai South,
Lanai Windward, Maui Central Valley North, Maui Central Valley
South, Maui Leeward West, Maui Windward West, Molokai Leeward
South, Molokai North, Molokai Southeast, Molokai West, Molokai
Windward, South Haleakala, South Maui/Upcountry, and Windward
Haleakala

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 340 miles south-southeast of Honolulu
- 16.7N 156.0W
- Storm Intensity 90 mph
- Movement West or 260 degrees at 5 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Hurricane Nolo is slowly moving west this morning and will pick up
speed as it strengthens into a major hurricane later tonight or early
Sunday. Nolo is forecast to accelerate west this weekend with a turn
toward the northwest and northwest expected Monday and Tuesday. While
the center will stay well south and west of the state, impacts will
extend far outside the center of the hurricane.

Bands of moderate to heavy showers and thunderstorms will bring an
additional 3 to 6 inches of rainfall to windward and southeast regions
of Big Island. Periods of moderate to locally heavy rain may spread
into Maui, bringing an additional 1 to 2 inches of rain. Localized
heavy rain could produce significant, life-threatening flooding and
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain. Terrain-enhanced
rainfall from outer rain bands may also reach the islands of Oahu and
Kauai.

A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Big Island as tropical
storm force winds and gusts, especially over complex terrain, continue
across that island today. A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Maui
County, where tropical storm force winds and gusts are occurring due
to terrain enhancement. Strong, gusty winds will affect all Hawaiian
Islands through the weekend. A Wind Advisory is in effect for the
islands of Oahu and Kauai.

Swells generated by Nolo will bring dangerously large, rough surf and
severe rip currents, especially for the east and southeast facing
shores of Big Island. A High Surf Advisory remains in effect for the
east and southeast and facing shores of Big Island as well as the east
facing shores of Maui, Molokai, Kauai and Oahu.

Tornadoes and waterspouts are possible near and over Big Island,
primarily to the right of the Nolo's track.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
Big Island and Maui. Remain well sheltered from dangerous wind having
possible significant impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Some damage to roofing and siding materials, along with damage
to porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few buildings
experiencing window, door, and garage door failures. Mobile
homes damaged, especially if unanchored. Unsecured lightweight
objects become dangerous projectiles.
- Several large trees snapped or uprooted, but with greater
numbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several
fences and roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. A few bridges, causeways, and access
routes impassable.
- Scattered power and communications outages, but more prevalent
in areas with above ground lines.

Potential indirect impacts from the main wind event are also now
unfolding across the rest of the state. Remain well sheltered from
hazardous wind having possible limited impacts.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
windward and southeast Big Island. Remain well guarded against
dangerous flood waters having possible significant impacts. If
realized, these impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals,
arroyos, and ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
windward and southeast Big Island and portions of Maui. Remain well
guarded against locally hazardous flood waters having possible
limited impacts.

* TORNADOES:
Potential impacts from tornadoes are still unfolding across Big
Island. Remain well braced against a tornado event having possible
limited impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

If you are relocating to safe shelter, leave as early as possible.
Allow extra time to reach your destination. Many roads and bridges
will be closed once strong winds arrive. Check the latest weather
forecast before departing and drive with caution.

If heading to a community shelter, become familiar with the shelter
rules before arrival, especially if you have special needs or have
pets. Take essential items with you from your Emergency Supplies Kit.

Failure to adequately shelter may result in serious injury or loss of
life. Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with any
orders that are issued. Remember, during the storm 9 1 1 Emergency
Services may not be able to immediately respond if conditions are
unsafe. This should be a big factor in your decision making.

Keep cell phones well charged. Cell phone chargers for automobiles
can be helpful, but be aware of your risk for deadly carbon monoxide
poisoning if your car is left idling in a garage or other poorly
ventilated area.

It is important to remain calm, informed, and focused during an
emergency. Be patient and helpful with those you encounter.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Storm surge is the leading killer associated with tropical storms and
hurricanes! Make sure you are in a safe area away from the surge
zone. Even if you are not in a surge-prone area, you could find
yourself cutoff by flood waters during and after the storm. Heed
evacuation orders issued by the local authorities.

Rapidly rising flood waters are deadly. If you are in a flood-prone
area, consider moving to higher ground. Never drive through a flooded
roadway. Remember, turn around don't drown!

If a Tornado Warning is issued for your area, be ready to shelter
quickly, preferably away from windows and in an interior room not
prone to flooding. If driving, scan the roadside for quick shelter
options.

If in a place that is vulnerable to high wind, such as near large
trees, a manufactured home, upper floors of a high-rise building, or
on a boat, consider moving to a safer shelter before the onset of
strong winds or flooding.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Honolulu HI around 5 PM HST, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

alerts.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 26 at 5:16AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
HLSHFO

This product covers the Hawaiian islands

**NOLO REMAINS NEARLY STATIONARY SOUTH OF THE BIG ISLAND**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Big Island East, Big Island Interior, Big Island North, Big
Island South, Big Island Southeast, Big Island Summits, Kohala,
and Kona
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Haleakala Summit,
Kahoolawe, Kipahulu, Lanai Leeward, Lanai Mauka, Lanai South,
Lanai Windward, Maui Central Valley North, Maui Central Valley
South, Maui Leeward West, Maui Windward West, Molokai Leeward
South, Molokai North, Molokai Southeast, Molokai West, Molokai
Windward, South Haleakala, South Maui/Upcountry, and Windward
Haleakala

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 340 miles south-southeast of Honolulu or about 200 miles
south of Hilo
- 16.9N 155.5W
- Storm Intensity 105 mph
- Movement Stationary

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Nearly stationary, Hurricane Nolo is expected to strengthen into a
major hurricane as it turns westward and accelerates later today and
Sunday. Nolo is forecast to track northward early next week and weaken.
While the center will stay well south and west of the state, impacts
will extend far outside the center of Nolo.

Bands of intense showers and thunderstorms will bring an additional
6 to 8 inches of rainfall with localized higher amounts of 10 inches
to windward and southeast portions of the Big Island. This heavy
rainfall will cause significant, life-threatening flash flooding and
mudslides, particularly in areas of steep terrain. Isolated heavy rain
will spread to Maui, bringing an additional 1 to 2 inches of rainfall
with locally higher amounts of 4 inches possible, especially over
steep terrain. Terrain-enhanced rainfall from outer rain bands may
also reach the rest of the state.

Tropical storm force winds and gusts continue across the Big Island,
and may reach hurricane strength today, especially over complex
terrain. A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Maui County, where
tropical storm force winds and gusts are occurring due to terrain
enhancements. Strong, gusty winds will affect all Hawaiian Islands
through the weekend, and a Wind Advisory is now in effect for the
remaining Hawaiian Islands.

Swells generated by Nolo will bring dangerously large, rough surf and
severe rip currents, especially for southeast and east facing shores
of Big Island and Maui. A High Surf Advisory remains in effect for
southeast and east facing shores of Big Island and Maui as well as
east facing shores of Molokai, Kauai and Oahu.

Tornadoes and waterspouts are possible near and over the Big Island,
primarily to the right of the track of Nolo.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
windward and southeast Big Island. Remain well guarded against
dangerous flood waters having possible significant impacts. If
realized, these impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals,
arroyos, and ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Potential impacts from the flooding rain are still unfolding across
windward and southeast Big Island and portions of Maui. Remain well
guarded against locally hazardous flood waters having possible limited
impacts.

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across Big
Island and Maui. Remain well sheltered from dangerous wind having
possible significant impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Some damage to roofing and siding materials, along with damage
to porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few buildings
experiencing window, door, and garage door failures. Mobile
homes damaged, especially if unanchored. Unsecured lightweight
objects become dangerous projectiles.
- Several large trees snapped or uprooted, but with greater
numbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several
fences and roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. A few bridges, causeways, and access
routes impassable.
- Scattered power and communications outages, but more prevalent
in areas with above ground lines.

Potential indirect impacts from the main wind event are also now
unfolding across the rest of the state. Remain well sheltered from
hazardous wind having possible limited impacts.


* SURGE:
Potential impacts from the main surge event are now unfolding across
southeast Big Island. Remain well away from locally hazardous surge
having possible limited impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across the Hawaiian islands, little to no impact is
anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Potential impacts from tornadoes are still unfolding across Big Island.
Remain well braced against a tornado event having possible limited
impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to stay inside and away from windows. Listen for
updates and be ready in case you lose electrical power. Keep a battery-
powered radio, charged cell phone and flashlight handy.

During the peak of the storm be ready to move quickly. Keep your
shoes on and rain gear handy. Boots and athletic shoes offer the best
foot protection if you become unexpectedly exposed to the weather.

Keep your cell phone charged and in power-saving mode. If you lose
power, use it sparingly and mainly for personal emergencies and
check-ins.

Do not venture outside while in the eye of a hurricane as any
improvement in weather will only be temporary. Once the eye passes,
conditions will become life threatening as winds immediately return
to dangerous speeds, so remain safely sheltered from the storm.

Do not be a thrill seeker or risk your life for senseless photos or
videos.

Quickly move to the safest place within your shelter if it begins to
fail, preferably an interior room on the lowest floor as long as
flooding is not a concern.

If you are prone to flooding or in an area under a storm surge watch
or warning, be prepared for the possibility of a quick and dramatic
rise in water levels.

If a tornado warning is issued for your area, quickly move to the
safest place within your shelter. Protect your head and body.

If an Extreme Wind Warning is issued for your area, move to the
safest place within your shelter. Take the same life-saving actions
as if it were a violent tornado.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Honolulu HI around 11 AM HST, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR EAST FACING SHORES OF KAUAI
AND OAHU THROUGH SUNDAY...

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY IN EFFECT FOR EAST AND SOUTHEAST FACING
SHORES OF MOLOKAI MAUI AND THE BIG ISLAND THROUGH SUNDAY...

.Hurricane Nolo is generating a moderate swell that is producing
advisory level surf along east and southeast facing shores of the
Big Island, Maui, and Molokai that will maintain tonight and then
diminish on Sunday as Nolo moves westward away from the islands.
Strengthening trades also cause building surf which peaks tonight
for east facing shorelines and begins to diminish on Sunday.

* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 9 to 12 ft.

* WHERE...East and southeast facing shores of the Big Island,
Maui, and Molokai.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate to high. Strong breaking waves and strong
currents will make swimming dangerous. Waves breaking in
channel entrances may make navigating the channels dangerous.
alerts.instruction:
Heed all advice from ocean safety officials. When in doubt, don't
go out.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 26 at 3:48AM HST until September 26 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
Hurricane Nolo remains nearly stationary south of the Big Island.
The possibility of heavy rain could lead to localized flooding over
portions of the Big Island and Maui.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Big Island, Maui, Lanai, Molokai, and Kahoolawe.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flood prone roads and other low lying areas may be closed
due to elevated runoff and overflowing streams. Urban areas may
receive more significant flooding and property damage due to rapid
runoff. Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The possibility remains for localized flooding over areas of the
Big Island and Maui due to heavy rain from slow moving Hurricane
Nolo to the south of the Big Island. Areas most at risk for
flooding are the windward and southeast portions of the Big
Island where the ground remains saturated after recent rains.
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM HST Sat Sep 26 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located a few hundred miles west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes,
Mexico, on Hurricane Odalys, located well west-southwest of the
southern tip of Baja California, and on Hurricane Nolo, located
south of the Big Island of Hawaii.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure is expected to form within the next day
or two about 1000 miles to the east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands. Environmental conditions are expected to be conducive for
development of the system, and a tropical depression is likely to
form during the early to middle part of next week. The system is
should move generally northeastward, and remain well east-southeast
of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Papin

aiBriefing: Huragan Nolo znajduje się bardzo blisko Waszej trasy — obecnie na południe od Big Island — i właśnie dlatego obowiązują ostrzeżenia (Tropical Storm Warning) dla Big Island oraz ostrzeżenia niższego stopnia (Watch) dla Maui, Lanai i Molokai, a także dla całego stanu ostrzeżenia przed silnym wiatrem, wysoką falą i powodzią. To poważne zagrożenie (poziom 4/5), realne w ciągu najbliższych 1-3 dni — jednak Wasza podróż zaczyna się dopiero za 5 dni (2 października), więc Nolo powinno oddalić się od Hawajów, zanim wylądujecie na Oahu. Mimo to warto śledzić sytuację do ostatniej chwili, bo prognozy huraganów bywają zmienne, a dodatkowo istnieje aż 70% szans, że w ciągu 7 dni uformuje się nowy system tropikalny daleko na wschód-południowy wschód od Hawajów — na razie zbyt daleko i zbyt wcześnie, by ocenić wpływ na Wasz przylot i pobyt na Big Island (5-8 października) czy Maui (8-12 października). Zalecamy sprawdzić aktualne alerty ponownie bliżej daty wylotu.
